ui.title: Help
ui.intro: Use Help in Steam's bottom bar for the focused control, or choose a topic below.

driver.title: Driver version
driver.text:
Choose the NVIDIA driver to prepare for the other SteamOS system slot. The current driver stays active until you restart. Labels show whether a version comes from Arch packages or a retained custom build. 'Needs build' means the plugin must build packages locally first.

A version already installed cannot be reinstalled. Changing this selection alone does not install anything.

recommended.title: Recommended (Arch)
recommended.text:
These versions are Arch Linux packages: the drivers to take. They avoid building custom packages from NVIDIA's installer. The NVIDIA kernel module still needs to be built for your SteamOS kernel.

They are labelled Arch whatever NVIDIA's own channel is for that release. It does not mean every listed version is the newest or the best choice for your GPU. The list includes older archived releases. 'Arch testing' identifies packages from an Arch testing repository; it is separate from NVIDIA's Beta channel.

nfb.title: New Feature Branch (NFB)
nfb.text:
NVIDIA releases classified as New Feature Branch, focused on newer features, that Arch does not package. They may need a local build.

A count of zero means no NVIDIA-only release is available in this channel right now. NFB releases that Arch packages are counted under Recommended (Arch).

beta.title: Beta
beta.text:
Pre-release drivers identified as Beta by NVIDIA. They may include new features or fixes and may also have regressions. This filter contains NVIDIA-source versions outside the Arch list.

These drivers may need a local build. 'Arch testing' is an Arch repository label and is not the same as NVIDIA Beta.

nvidia_recommended.title: NVIDIA Recommended
nvidia_recommended.text:
NVIDIA releases marked Recommended, its production branch, that Arch does not package. They need a local build before installation.

A release NVIDIA does not classify in any channel is always shown in the picker.

filters.title: Filter by source / channel
filters.text:
These switches control which categories appear in the driver picker. They do not install, remove or change the active driver.

Counts describe available versions by source: every Arch package is counted under Recommended (Arch), whatever its NVIDIA channel, and NVIDIA-only releases are counted in their NVIDIA channel. Availability also depends on the current package and custom-build catalogues. Use the Help action on an individual filter for its explanation.

channel.title: Update channel
channel.text:
Choose the category used for the default driver selection, update notices and the 'Up to date' comparison. All channels compares the available categories. Needs build selects versions requiring local package creation.

This setting does not install updates automatically. The source filters separately control what you can see in the picker.

builds.title: Show exact builds (-N)
builds.text:
Show individual Arch package revisions, such as 615.78.08-1 and 615.78.08-2, instead of combining them under one NVIDIA version. The number after the dash is the package revision, not a new NVIDIA driver version.

This changes the list display and lets you select an exact package revision; it does not change your installed driver.

install.title: Install driver
install.text:
The plugin prepares and validates a compressed system image on /home, then writes it to the inactive SteamOS A/B slot. That slot's previous contents are replaced. Your currently running system is retained for rollback. Restart after preparation completes to use the new driver.

The plugin supports compatible A/B layouts with the original root size as well as previously enlarged 8 GB roots. It uses the detected target size and checks free space; it does not resize partitions. Custom versions also need time and space for a local package build.

rollback.title: Return to previous system
rollback.text:
Select the retained previous system for the next boot, after verifying that both saved system identities still match. Restart to switch to it. This switches the saved system slot, not just one driver package.

Rollback may be unavailable if an OS update or another operation has replaced the saved system. A later driver preparation overwrites the inactive slot.

reboot.title: Reboot now
reboot.text: Restart the PC into the system selected by the completed driver preparation or rollback. Until you restart, the current driver remains loaded. Save any open work before restarting.

log.title: Driver update log
log.text:
Open the saved operation log in a larger window. Live mode always follows the newest line at the bottom. Press the left stick (L3) to browse history with the right stick; press L3 again to return to Live. In history mode you can also use the mouse wheel or keyboard. Click the log to switch modes when using a mouse.

The log remains available after restarting Decky. Very large logs show their recent portion and the full file path. Opening or closing the viewer does not start, cancel or change the operation.

notes.title: Release notes
notes.text: Read NVIDIA's published changes for the selected driver. Notes may not be available for every archived package. Opening this window does not install the driver. Plugin release history is a separate section in Settings.

reconnect.title: Reconnect
reconnect.text: Refresh the status of the driver operation after a connection problem. A running operation belongs to systemd and can continue while Decky reloads. Reconnecting observes that existing operation; it does not start a second installation.

settings.title: Plugin settings
settings.text:
View plugin release history, check plugin releases and access project links. Plugin updates replace the Decky plugin itself; NVIDIA driver updates are a separate action on the main panel.

Plugin installation is blocked while a driver operation is running or its status is unknown.

history.title: Plugin release history
history.text: Read changes made to the Decky plugin. This is separate from NVIDIA driver release notes and does not change the installed driver.

plugin.title: Plugin updates and project links
plugin.text: Choose a published plugin release and let Decky install its ZIP, or open the project's feedback and issue links. This updates the plugin, not the NVIDIA driver. The configured repository determines which releases are offered.

support.title: Support
support.text: Open the plugin author's support links. This section does not change your driver or system configuration.

v0_5_0.title: What's new in 0.5.0
items: More reliable driver changes: your SteamOS configuration is now preserved, and the initramfs build error (blake2b_generic) that could stop an update is handled
A driver already installed is now explained and refused instead of failing silently
New log viewer: scrollable, kept after Decky restarts, with L3 to browse the history
Built-in contextual help on every control, available in English, French and Spanish
Driver picker reorganized: Recommended (Arch) lists the Arch packages to take, and NVIDIA-only versions are split into Recommended, NFB and Beta, with live counts
NVIDIA release notes and channels now cover both the production and New Feature Branch catalogs

v0_4_0.title: What's new in 0.4.0
items: No more 8 GiB root requirement: the driver is now prepared in the inactive SteamOS A/B system and activated by a reboot, the current system is kept as a fallback
New rollback button to go back to the previous system
Compiled builds no longer in use are cleaned up automatically, and builds from earlier versions are migrated
Redesigned driver picker with the source of each version shown on a second line
Notifications now use the NVIDIA icon

v0_3_0.title: What's new in 0.3.0
items: New Settings page: plugin self-update, bug report, feature request, support the development
Build a driver version Arch never packaged, straight from Arch's own packaging repos — see the new section under the version picker
